sections.title: 1. Executive Verdict
sections.text: Completed conditional review: BQS 5.24, growth-quality GQS 6.05, IAS 4.51. The diagnostic-products business has a tangible plant runway, but trading dominates revenue, cash conversion is modest and expansion creates financing risk. Central modeled IRR is 12.7%; a bear recapitalization materially damages shareholders. [S1–S4, M1]

sections.title: 2. Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: As of 20 October 2026. Avience Biomedicals Limited, ISIN INE0V9I01017, NSE symbol AVIENCE, listed on NSE Emerge on June 25, 2026. Annual capital plus fresh IPO reconciles to 5,485,056 shares; the current exchange master corroborates the 600-share lot. Consolidated FY26 uses the corrected August 25 baseline, not uncorrected July results. October 19 close ₹258.10 is not live or guaranteed executable. All four gates are assessed separately. [S1–S3, M1, M_SECURITY_SPEC]

sections.title: 3. Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: GOV 5, MOAT 5, REV 7, DUR 6, CAP 5, CASH 4, BAL 5, EXEC 5 and EARN 6. REV uses the latest comparable full-year growth of 16.07%, not acquisition-affected two-year CAGR. IAS factors are R 4, D 3, P 5 and L 7. Exact weighted arithmetic and contradictory evidence appear in the factor audit. All confidence is Medium; forecasts remain conditional.

sections.title: 4. Business Overview
sections.text: The group supplies and manufactures diagnostic reagents, rapid tests and instruments and distributes third-party products. July call disclosure says approximately 26.99% of turnover was manufacturing, around 72% trading and the balance service. Manufactured reagents/consumables, rapid cards and instruments were about 14.62%, 9.15% and 3.21% respectively. This is not predominantly proprietary biotechnology IP. DR Meditech became a 99.99% subsidiary August 8,2023; FY24 consolidation therefore does not represent a full-year unchanged group. [S1, S3, S4]

sections.title: 5. Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: Manufacturing licences, service responsiveness and reagent-linked instrument placement can create customer friction, but management’s five-year reagent-rental agreements and four-hour service commitment are claims, not verified retention economics. The 72% trading share limits a broad IP-moat interpretation. Prospectus parent-company top 10 customers were 56.82% of FY25 revenue and 46.44% in ten months to January 2026; those figures must not be relabelled consolidated concentration. Supplier concentration and third-party instruments add dependencies. [S3, S4]

sections.title: 6. Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Consolidated revenue rose from ₹23.9640 crore FY24 to ₹45.2359 crore FY25 and ₹52.5058 crore FY26. The two-year reported CAGR is about 48.0%, but FY24 contains only part-year acquired DR Meditech; FY26 growth is a more modest 16.07%. Management’s July call forecast of at least 60% FY27 growth, ₹47 crore orders and 50:50 manufacturing/trading target are forward-looking claims, not audited sales or confirmed cash receipts. Do not annualize ten-month IPO figures or call growth wholly organic. [S1, S3, S4]

sections.title: 7. Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: FY25–26 CWIP-inclusive ΔNOPAT/ΔIC proxy is 13.7% at 25.17% tax, versus 25.9% if CWIP is excluded. The former is the primary measure because cash already committed matters. It straddles an assumed 12–16% capital cost, supporting mixed rather than exceptional returns. Prospectus new-plant budget ₹30.1846 crore is funded by IPO ₹14.0453 crore, internal ₹4.1393 crore and borrowing ₹12 crore. FY27 WC stock ₹20.4939 crore requires IPO ₹5 crore, internal ₹8.4939 crore and borrowing ₹7 crore. These are plans, not funded completions. October commissioning was targeted, but no completion evidence was established in reviewed announcements. [S1–S4] FY26 plant-specific CWIP is identified as ₹12.8528 crore in annual note 14. Other capital advances include ₹0.7952 crore for separate land awaiting possession, so they are not all netted from the plant cost. Base year-five sales are about ₹105.6 crore, well below management’s unverified ₹250 crore peak-capacity claim; neither that claim nor 60% guidance is needed for the central growth path. [S1, S4]

sections.title: 8. Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: August 25 revision removes ₹3.3755 crore intercompany loans/advances and matching liabilities omitted because workbook links were removed; profit/equity were unchanged. This is a disclosed control failure with a corrected usable baseline, not evidence of profit fabrication. September 30 AGM filing appoints M.A.M and Associates as statutory auditor in place of retiring Haribhakti for the next five AGMs; internal and secretarial appointments are separate. Do not misdescribe the change as an unexplained midyear resignation. Related-party remuneration remains material and needs benchmarking; prior July 16 auditor report was superseded for the corrected consolidation, not assumed to cover all subsequent events. [S1, S2, S5]

sections.title: 9. Financial Forensics
sections.text: FY25–26 cumulative CFO/PAT is approximately 0.587; CFO less cash capex including advances totals negative ₹13.4466 crore. FY26 inventory and receivables absorbed ₹8.1459 crore, partly offset by payables. Debt cash inflow ₹6.7766 crore helped finance the shortfall. Restated IPO FY25 PAT/CFO ₹7.2318/3.6063 crore differs from annual comparative ₹7.0990/3.3943 crore; keep the restated table separate rather than splice ratios. The corrected intercompany elimination does not change equity or profit and is not double-subtracted from CFO. [S1–S3] The revised opening WC is ₹29.3175 crore after operating advances and liabilities. March IPO prepaid costs ₹0.3623 crore are excluded from WC and recouped once; opening income-tax ₹3.3086 crore and interest ₹0.1676 crore are paid separately. Cash equivalents exclude ₹0.6597 crore other bank deposits. These bridges avoid free cash arising from omitted claims or double-charged issue costs. [S1, S3] Opening-claim audit: operating statutory, payroll and expense liabilities of ₹0.8867 crore and current employee/expense provisions of ₹0.0375 crore are already included in opening and forecast operating WC. They are not charged again as separate debt. Opening tax/interest settlement remains ₹3.1139 crore net of IPO prepaid reimbursement. Noncurrent employee liabilities of ₹0.1597 crore are outside operating WC and are now deducted once from terminal equity, held at the opening net obligation with no assumed plan-asset recovery. Future service cost remains within forecast operating expenses. The ₹0.1864 crore opening deferred-tax liability is separately reserved once at terminal. Forecast tax at 25.17% of future positive PBT does not model legacy tax-basis reversals; this reserve is a conservative timing assumption, not a cash tax currently due. Deferred-tax assets receive no cash credit. If legacy reversal is explicitly included in future cash taxes, this reserve must be released to avoid duplication. Existing bank principal remains in the debt schedule and terminal debt; no duplicate current-maturity deduction is made. [S1]

sections.title: 10. Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text: Actual-opening annual cash, debt and dilution scenarios give bear/base/bull equity IRRs of -14.5%/12.7%/35.7%. Base assumes 15% sales growth, 23% EBIT margin and 11-times terminal EV/EBIT. Working capital, plant costs, tax/interest claims, known repayment steps, new debt and fallback equity are linked. The 15% hurdle requires about 12.1 times terminal EV/EBIT at central operations. Prior 13-times exit remains an optimistic sensitivity. [S1–S4, M1] The terminal bridge additionally retains the audited legacy employee and deferred-tax claims; the annual operating and financing schedules are unchanged. [S1]

sections.title: 11. Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: Loss mechanism: plant delay or low utilization increases carrying cost, while government-order growth lengthens collections and requires debt before cash realization. Management explicitly said larger WC needs were not fully available and facilities remained subject to bank approvals. A 10% impairment of FY26 receivables plus inventory (₹38.1925 crore) would be ₹3.8193 crore, roughly 43.6% of PAT or 12.2% of equity, before tax; this is a stress, not a prediction. Increasing manufacturing mix may help margins, but approvals, product demand and debt service must be demonstrated. [S1, S4] The ordinary bear requires approximately ₹4.80 crore rescue equity at half the observed quote, producing 54.4% terminal equity loss. Cash credit ₹11.6721 crore plus related demand borrowing ₹2.4093 crore are specifically tested as immediately recalled, not treated as perpetual committed capital.

sections.title: 12. 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: Five-year 5× and 10× equity outcomes require 37.97% and 58.49% annualized returns. A one-year 60% sales aspiration is not a five-year per-share forecast. Even the bull requires 25% sustained sales growth, 27% EBIT margin, improved working-capital intensity and a 15-times exit. Dilution and debt claims are deducted. Five times is demanding and ten times unsupported by the modeled operating path; neither is assigned a precise probability.

sections.title: 13. Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Monitor corrected balance-sheet publication, consolidation controls, ageing/expiry, product registrations, receivable collections, borrowing, IPO deployment and repeat reagent revenues. Next-session NSE REG1 alerts, effective October 21,2026: Less than 100 unique PAN traded in previous 30 days; SME scrip is not regularly traded. These caution flags do not establish wrongdoing or actual missing trading sessions. [M_REG1, M_REG1_FORMAT]

sections.title: 14. Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Conditional watchlist, not a buy recommendation. The corrected financial baseline is usable, but weak conversion and an expansion financed partly by demand credit make stress outcomes material. Investment consideration would require evidence of commissioning, realized mix/collections and adequate finance at the observed valuation.

sections.title: 15. Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: Reviewed annual and revised financial notes, June final prospectus, July earnings call, September auditor appointment and October 1 conference outcome. The latter confirms participation and reports no new price-sensitive information; it does not establish commissioning. No primary current peer multiple is claimed. Remaining unknowns are actual deployment, capital-advance allocation, manufacturing yields, sanctioned additional credit and order-to-cash conversion, all separated from modeled assumptions. [S1–S6]

assumptions: Money is INR crore and shares are crore shares. Five full modeled years approximate October 2026 to October 2031. Historical FY26 consolidated accounts plus known IPO are the opening bridge, not an observed October balance sheet. No interim dividends are assumed.

Operating WC starts at 29.3175: inventory and receivables less trade payables 28.7179, plus supplier advances 0.2191, employee advances 0.0979, government balances 0.7859, earnest money 0.1657, ordinary prepaid expenses 0.0192 and other advances 0.2360; less operating current liabilities 0.8867 and employee provisions 0.0375. IPO prepaid expenses 0.3623 and interest receivable 0.1505 are not operating WC.

Cash equivalents 2.2747 exclude other bank deposits 0.6597, including restricted/lien deposits. Net IPO cash 26.2674 is credited once. March prepaid IPO costs 0.3623 are recouped because the prospectus explicitly permits reimbursement from gross proceeds; otherwise deducting all issue costs twice would understate cash. A no-reimbursement sensitivity is shown.

Opening income-tax provision 3.3086 and accrued borrowing/MSME interest 0.1676 are conservatively paid before forecast year one. Future modeled taxes and interest cover only forecast earnings and debt, so those claims are not duplicated.

Plant budget 30.1846 less March project-specific CWIP 12.8528 gives remaining cash cost 17.3318. Annual note 14 explicitly identifies all CWIP with the YEIDA biochemistry analyser plant. Capital advances 2.0527 include 0.7952 for a different land allotment awaiting possession; no automatic credit for the remainder is taken. A 1.2575 credit and full-project-cost alternative are separate sensitivities.

Base sales growth 15% is close to the latest full-year comparable growth of 16.07%, far below management’s 60% one-year aspiration. Base EBIT margin 23% is below the historical 26.12% operating margin, allowing for depreciation, launch costs and trading mix. Forecast year-five sales of about 105.6 do not require the claimed 250 crore plant peak, which is not independently validated.

Project spending is 70%/30% over the first two years. Growth capex is the greater of this schedule and incremental sales divided by assumed fixed-asset turnover; maintenance equals depreciation. Ten-year depreciation with a half-year convention is an analyst assumption, not company guidance. Cash WC changes from the explicit opening stock each year.

Initial SIDBI debt 9.545 has disclosed stepped monthly repayments. Remaining first five annual buckets are 0.66, 0.705, 1.60, 2.40 and 2.40. Other term principal is 5.3084; year one uses remaining disclosed current maturities of 0.9647, then 1.085925 annually as a bounded approximation. The resulting total principal schedule is 1.6247, 1.790925, 2.685925, 3.485925 and 3.485925. Later years align to a synthetic five-year period, not exact contractual dates.

Existing cash credit and related demand loans are not falsely amortized as term loans. They remain subject to renewal/call risk, tested separately. Future total-debt capacity is assumed at 30% of sales; this is not a claimed sanctioned limit. Above that constraint, modeled cash deficits require equity issued at half the observed quote. If funding fails, operations must be curtailed or recovery worsens.

Interest uses opening debt less half scheduled principal plus half new drawings, solving financing circularity. Cash tax is 25.17% of positive PBT. Cash floor is 5% of revenue. Terminal EV is year-five EBIT times the assumed multiple, less bank debt, plus cash above the floor, divided by modeled diluted shares.

Exit multiples 8/11/15 are explicit estimates, not measured peer multiples. The central 11 times compares with about 10.6 times historical operating EBIT using the IPO-adjusted funding bridge, before assuming future growth. The former 13-times central exit is retained as an optimistic sensitivity. Scenario probabilities are optional and not assigned.

The all-demand-credit call sensitivity prohibits replacement borrowing; any funding shortfall must be met by conditional equity or curtailment. This distinguishes a true credit withdrawal from a repayment refinanced by another lender.

Opening-claim audit: operating statutory, payroll and expense liabilities of ₹0.8867 crore and current employee/expense provisions of ₹0.0375 crore are already included in opening and forecast operating WC. They are not charged again as separate debt. Opening tax/interest settlement remains ₹3.1139 crore net of IPO prepaid reimbursement. Noncurrent employee liabilities of ₹0.1597 crore are outside operating WC and are now deducted once from terminal equity, held at the opening net obligation with no assumed plan-asset recovery. Future service cost remains within forecast operating expenses. The ₹0.1864 crore opening deferred-tax liability is separately reserved once at terminal. Forecast tax at 25.17% of future positive PBT does not model legacy tax-basis reversals; this reserve is a conservative timing assumption, not a cash tax currently due. Deferred-tax assets receive no cash credit. If legacy reversal is explicitly included in future cash taxes, this reserve must be released to avoid duplication. Existing bank principal remains in the debt schedule and terminal debt; no duplicate current-maturity deduction is made.

GOV.reason: Consolidation error disclosed and corrected with no PAT/equity effect; contrary: removed workbook links and related pay constrain control confidence.

MOAT.reason: Licensed products and reagent/service relationships support positioning; contrary:72% trading and concentrated parent customers limit IP/pricing claims.

REV.reason: Latest full-year same-scope growth of 16.07% maps to 7 and is used as the comparable-growth proxy. The reported 48% two-year CAGR starts from a partial-year acquired subsidiary and is not used to award a higher score. This is a one-year proxy with Medium confidence, not an invented organic CAGR.

DUR.reason: Specific plant, capacity and IPO allocation provide runway; contrary: commissioning and extra working-capital funding not established.

CAP.reason: CWIP-inclusive incremental proxy about 13.7% is mixed against 12–16% hurdle; excluding CWIP improves but ignores committed capital.

CASH.reason: Two-year CFO/PAT0.587 and large negative CFO-minus-capex; contrary: positive CFO improved and IPO offers new resources, not yet proven conversion.

BAL.reason: IPO net ₹26.2674 crore adds funding potential; contrary:pre-IPO debt ₹28.9348 crore, high working-capital intensity and conditional additional bank lines.

EXEC.reason: Manufacturing output/utilization and revenue grew; contrary: new plant schedule and intended manufacturing mix still require execution.

EARN.reason: PAT grew 23.3% and operating margin improved; contrary: post-IPO dilution, prior tax adjustments and trading/product mix make extrapolation uncertain.

R.reason: Central conditional five-year IRR 12.72% after all identified opening claims is -2.28 percentage points below/above the 15% hurdle, mapping to R=4. Forecasts and terminal tax timing remain assumptions.

D.reason: Ordinary bear loses 54.4% of quoted equity value and needs about ₹4.80 crore conditional equity. Demand-credit withdrawal and plant overruns materially worsen the funding path; rescue is not assured.

P.reason: The 15% hurdle needs about 12.1 times terminal EV/EBIT at central operations versus an 11-times model assumption. This is a fair-execution case with little room for commissioning, collection or margin misses, not a conservative-margin-of-safety setup.

L.reason: All 60 sessions are observed. Conservative daily turnover ₹75.98145 lakh implies 1.32 days at 5% participation; 2%/10% imply 3.29/0.66 days. Starting band 9 is reduced to 7 for the less-than-100-PAN caution, ₹154,860 lot and unobserved spread/depth.

gates.reason: The disclosed consolidation error was corrected without changing profit or equity. Related remuneration and concentrated control warrant scrutiny, but the reviewed material does not substantiate severe diversion or minority abuse.

August corrected consolidation is the primary baseline; removed workbook links explain a disclosed ₹3.3755 crore intercompany elimination correction. Annual/restated comparative differences are not spliced. Opening operating, tax, interest and IPO-prepaid balances are explicitly reconciled.

Known IPO and existing assets support a central plan, while ordinary bear requires conditional equity and demand credit can be recalled. SIDBI repayment steps and current maturities are incorporated; future lines are not assumed committed. Severe financing failure can cause permanent loss.

Dated official quote, 600-share lot and 60 observed sessions support a reference test. Three whole lots cost ₹464,580 versus a ₹5 lakh reference. Limited PAN breadth, circuits and absent live depth mean liquidation capacity is not guaranteed.
